title: Payment webhook delivered more than once
context_text: The payment provider re-delivers a webhook after a non-2xx or a timeout, so the handler runs twice and the customer is charged twice
solution_text: Persist the provider's event id and check it before any side effect. Make the handler idempotent at the write, not at the entry point, so a retry that gets further than the last one still cannot double-apply.
source: public: payment-provider webhook delivery semantics are documented as at-least-once by Stripe, PayPal and Adyen alike

title: Consumer group rebalance loses in-flight messages
context_text: A deploy triggers a consumer group rebalance and messages that were fetched but not yet committed are reprocessed or dropped
solution_text: Commit offsets only after processing completes, not on fetch. Add a rebalance listener that finishes or abandons in-flight work before partitions are revoked.
source: public: Kafka consumer group rebalance protocol and offset-commit semantics

title: Connection pool exhausted during a retry storm
context_text: A brief database blip causes clients to retry, the retries amplify, and the pool is starved long after the original fault cleared
solution_text: Bound retries with jittered exponential backoff and set a pool acquisition timeout so callers fail fast instead of queueing. Add a circuit breaker so a sustained fault stops generating load.
source: public: well-documented cascading-failure pattern; see AWS Architecture Blog on exponential backoff and jitter

title: Token validation fails intermittently from clock drift
context_text: JWT validation rejects valid tokens on some hosts because container clocks drift from the issuer's clock
solution_text: Allow a small leeway when validating exp and nbf, and run time sync on hosts. Do not widen leeway past a minute or so; fix the clocks instead.
source: public: RFC 7519 section 4.1.4 explicitly allows for clock-skew leeway

title: Retries synchronize and hammer the recovering service
context_text: Every client retries on the same fixed schedule, so the service is hit by a synchronized wave the moment it starts recovering
solution_text: Add full jitter to backoff so retry times spread out. Fixed or purely exponential backoff without randomization reproduces the thundering herd it was meant to avoid.
source: public: AWS Architecture Blog, 'Exponential Backoff And Jitter'

title: Cache stampede when a hot key expires
context_text: A widely-read cache entry expires and every concurrent request misses at once, all recomputing the same expensive value
solution_text: Serialize recomputation behind a per-key lock, or serve stale while one worker refreshes. Randomize TTLs so keys written together do not expire together.
source: public: cache stampede / dogpile effect is a long-documented pattern

title: Load balancer idle timeout shorter than keep-alive
context_text: Requests intermittently fail with connection reset because the client reuses a pooled connection the load balancer already closed
solution_text: Set the client's keep-alive idle timeout strictly below the load balancer's, so the client retires connections first. Do not rely on retry to paper over it.
source: public: documented for AWS ELB/ALB, nginx and Envoy keep-alive tuning

title: SIGTERM kills requests still in flight
context_text: A rolling deploy terminates pods and long-running requests are cut off, surfacing as client-side 502s during every release
solution_text: Handle SIGTERM by stopping new work, draining in-flight requests, then exiting. Set the orchestrator's grace period longer than the slowest expected request.
source: public: Kubernetes pod termination lifecycle documentation

title: Readiness probe wired to a dependency check
context_text: A brief database outage makes every replica report unhealthy at once, so the orchestrator restarts them all and the outage gets worse
solution_text: Keep liveness independent of dependencies; only readiness should test them. A dependency being down means stop sending traffic, not restart the process.
source: public: Kubernetes probe documentation distinguishes liveness from readiness for exactly this reason

title: Floating point used for money
context_text: Totals drift by fractions of a cent and reconciliation fails, because amounts were stored and summed as floats
solution_text: Store money as integer minor units or a fixed-point decimal type. Never use binary floating point for currency arithmetic.
source: public: IEEE 754 cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly; standard financial-systems guidance

title: Mutable default argument shared across calls
context_text: A Python function with a list or dict default accumulates state between calls because the default is evaluated once at definition
solution_text: Default to None and construct the container inside the function body.
source: public: documented in the Python language reference on default parameter values

title: Timezone arithmetic breaks across a DST boundary
context_text: Adding 24 hours to a local timestamp lands on the wrong wall-clock hour when the interval crosses a daylight-saving transition
solution_text: Do arithmetic in UTC and convert to local only for display, or use a library that applies calendar-aware addition with a real timezone database.
source: public: IANA tz database semantics; standard datetime-handling guidance

title: N+1 queries from lazy ORM relationship access
context_text: A list endpoint issues one query per row because a related object is accessed inside the loop, so latency scales with result size
solution_text: Eager-load the relation in the initial query, or batch-load related rows by id in one round trip.
source: public: N+1 select problem is documented across Hibernate, ActiveRecord and SQLAlchemy

title: Missing index on a foreign key column
context_text: Deletes on the parent table get slower as the child table grows, because each delete scans the child to enforce the constraint
solution_text: Index the referencing column. Most databases index the primary key side automatically but not the referencing side.
source: public: PostgreSQL documentation notes that referencing columns are not indexed automatically

title: ADD COLUMN NOT NULL fails on a populated table
context_text: A migration that adds a non-nullable column succeeds on an empty test database and fails in production with 'column contains null values'
solution_text: Supply a server-side default so existing rows backfill, or add the column nullable, backfill, then set NOT NULL.
source: public: standard SQL DDL semantics; reproduced identically on PostgreSQL and MySQL

title: Schema migration locks a table during deploy
context_text: An index build or column rewrite takes an exclusive lock and blocks reads and writes for the duration on a large table
solution_text: Build indexes concurrently where the engine supports it, and split the change into expand, backfill, contract phases so the old and new application versions both work mid-migration.
source: public: PostgreSQL CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY documentation; expand/contract is standard practice

title: Unbounded result set loaded into memory
context_text: An endpoint that was fine in testing exhausts memory in production because it materializes every matching row before serializing
solution_text: Paginate with a hard maximum page size, and stream or cursor through large result sets rather than collecting them.
source: public: standard API pagination guidance; a recurring cause of OOM incidents

title: Offset pagination skips or repeats rows
context_text: Paging through a list with OFFSET returns duplicates or misses records when rows are inserted or deleted between pages
solution_text: Order by a total, stable key and paginate by cursor on that key. If OFFSET must be used, add a unique tiebreaker to the sort so the order is deterministic.
source: public: keyset vs offset pagination is well documented; ordering without a unique tiebreaker is not stable

title: Read-modify-write loses a concurrent update
context_text: Two processes read a record, each change a different field, and the second write silently reverts the first change
solution_text: Update the specific fields in the database rather than writing back a whole object, or use optimistic concurrency with a version column and retry on conflict.
source: public: lost update is a classic transaction anomaly, defined in the SQL standard's isolation discussion

title: Non-atomic check-then-insert races under concurrency
context_text: Code checks whether a row exists and inserts if not; under concurrent requests both checks pass and one insert violates a unique constraint
solution_text: Use an atomic upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) so the database resolves the race, rather than racing two round trips against it.
source: public: PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT documentation exists specifically for this pattern

title: Counter increments lost under concurrent updates
context_text: A counter read into the application, incremented, and written back loses increments when requests overlap
solution_text: Increment in the database (SET n = n + 1) so the operation is atomic, instead of reading and writing from application memory.
source: public: standard consequence of read-modify-write without isolation

title: Retry after a committed write duplicates the effect
context_text: A client times out waiting for a response, retries, and the operation is applied twice because the first attempt had already committed
solution_text: Accept a client-supplied idempotency key, store it with the result, and return the original result on replay. Timeouts cannot distinguish 'never happened' from 'happened but the reply was lost'.
source: public: idempotency keys are documented practice at Stripe, Square and AWS

title: Docker layer cache invalidated by copying source too early
context_text: Every build reinstalls all dependencies because source files are copied before the dependency manifest, invalidating the cached layer
solution_text: Copy the dependency manifest and install first, then copy source. Ordering instructions from least to most frequently changed keeps the cache useful.
source: public: Docker documentation on build cache and layer invalidation

title: Secrets baked into an image layer
context_text: A credential passed as a build argument or copied in and later deleted is still recoverable from the image history
solution_text: Never pass secrets as build args or COPY them in. Inject at runtime from the platform's secret store, or use a build-time secret mount that leaves no layer.
source: public: Docker documentation warns that build args and deleted files persist in layer history

title: Container runs as root by default
context_text: A compromised process in the container has root in the namespace, widening the blast radius of any application-level vulnerability
solution_text: Create an unprivileged user in the image and switch to it with USER before the entrypoint. Drop capabilities the process does not need.
source: public: standard container-hardening guidance; CIS Docker Benchmark

title: Dependency floor pin resolves to an unexpected version
context_text: A build that worked yesterday breaks today because an unpinned transitive or floor-pinned dependency released a new version
solution_text: Pin direct dependencies exactly and use a lock file for transitive ones, so a rebuild resolves to the same versions that were tested.
source: public: standard reproducible-build guidance across pip-tools, Poetry, npm and Cargo

title: New library version silently drops an old runtime
context_text: A dependency bump fails only on the oldest supported runtime in the CI matrix, because the new release raised its minimum version
solution_text: Check the package's requires-python or engines constraint against the whole support matrix before bumping, and let CI cover the oldest version.
source: public: PyPI requires-python and npm engines metadata exist to express exactly this

title: YAML parses unquoted country code NO as false
context_text: A configuration value like NO, ON or YES becomes a boolean instead of the intended string, corrupting config in a way that raises no error
solution_text: Quote such values, or use a YAML 1.2 parser where only true and false are booleans. Validate config against a schema so a type change fails loudly.
source: public: the YAML 1.1 boolean resolver treats y/yes/no/on/off as booleans; widely known as the 'Norway problem'

title: Timestamps stored without timezone information
context_text: Times are stored as naive local timestamps, so records written from hosts in different regions cannot be ordered or compared reliably
solution_text: Store instants in UTC with an explicit timezone-aware type, and convert only at the presentation boundary.
source: public: standard guidance; PostgreSQL timestamptz vs timestamp semantics

title: String comparison used for authentication secrets
context_text: Comparing a token with an ordinary equality check leaks timing information proportional to the length of the matching prefix
solution_text: Use a constant-time comparison for secrets, or compare a hash. For passwords, use a purpose-built KDF whose verify function is already constant time.
source: public: timing attacks on non-constant-time comparison are well documented; hmac.compare_digest exists for this

title: Password hashed with a fast general-purpose hash
context_text: Credentials stored with SHA-256 or MD5 are brute-forced quickly if the database leaks, because the hash is designed to be fast
solution_text: Use a memory-hard password KDF such as argon2id, bcrypt or scrypt with tuned cost parameters, and a per-credential salt.
source: public: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet

title: User input interpolated into a query string
context_text: Building SQL by concatenating request values allows an attacker to alter the query's structure
solution_text: Pass values as bound parameters so they can never be parsed as SQL. This applies to LIKE patterns and ORDER BY targets too, which need an allowlist rather than interpolation.
source: public: OWASP Top 10 A03 Injection

title: Path built from user input escapes the intended directory
context_text: A filename taken from a request contains traversal sequences and resolves outside the directory the code intended to serve
solution_text: Resolve the final path and verify it is contained within the base directory. Reject separators outright rather than relying on basename, which only recognizes the host platform's separator.
source: public: OWASP path traversal guidance; CWE-22

title: Unbounded request body read into memory
context_text: A large upload exhausts memory because the whole body is buffered before any size check happens
solution_text: Enforce a maximum body size at the server and check bytes actually received, not just a declared Content-Length, since chunked encoding can omit it.
source: public: standard web-server hardening; Content-Length is optional under HTTP chunked transfer-encoding

title: Client-supplied value logged without sanitization
context_text: A header echoed straight into logs lets an attacker inject newlines and forge log entries, or emit terminal escape sequences
solution_text: Bound the length and restrict the character set of any client value used in logs, and prefer structured logging where the encoder escapes control characters.
source: public: OWASP log injection guidance; CWE-117

title: Error message discloses internal detail
context_text: An unhandled exception returns a stack trace or SQL fragment to the client, revealing schema and file paths
solution_text: Map internal errors to generic messages with a correlation id, and log the detail server-side. Distinguish not-found from forbidden deliberately, since the difference can itself confirm a resource exists.
source: public: OWASP guidance on improper error handling; CWE-209

title: Rate limiter state held per process
context_text: An in-memory rate limiter allows roughly N times the intended rate once the service runs on N replicas
solution_text: Hold the counter in a shared store with atomic increment and TTL, or enforce the limit at a gateway in front of the replicas.
source: public: standard consequence of local state in a horizontally scaled service

title: High-cardinality label on a metric
context_text: Using a user id, trace id or raw URL path as a metric label creates a new time series per value and overwhelms the metrics backend
solution_text: Label with the route template rather than the concrete path, and keep identifiers in logs or traces where cardinality is expected.
source: public: Prometheus documentation warns explicitly about label cardinality

title: CORS preflight response cached with the wrong origin
context_text: An intermediate cache serves a preflight response computed for one origin to a request from another, causing intermittent CORS failures
solution_text: Include Origin in the Vary header on any response whose CORS headers depend on it, so caches key the entry correctly.
source: public: Fetch standard and MDN CORS documentation on Vary: Origin

title: Concurrent token refresh causes intermittent 401s
context_text: Several requests notice an expired access token at once and each starts a refresh; the later refreshes invalidate the token the earlier ones just obtained
solution_text: Serialize refresh behind a single-flight lock so concurrent callers await one refresh, and tolerate a short overlap window where both old and new tokens are accepted.
source: public: documented consequence of refresh-token rotation; single-flight is the standard remedy

title: Long-lived connections pin to stale DNS records
context_text: A failover changes a DNS record but clients keep using the old address because a resolved address was cached for the process lifetime
solution_text: Honour record TTLs rather than resolving once at startup, and recycle pooled connections periodically so a failover is picked up.
source: public: JVM and various runtimes historically cached DNS indefinitely; documented operational hazard

title: Unicode normalization difference defeats an identity check
context_text: Two strings that display identically compare as different because one uses precomposed characters and the other combining marks
solution_text: Normalize to a single form before comparing or storing identifiers. Be aware that case folding and normalization can map distinct inputs together, which matters for uniqueness checks.
source: public: Unicode Standard Annex 15 on normalization forms

title: Byte-length limit truncates a multi-byte character
context_text: Truncating a string to a byte limit splits a multi-byte character and produces invalid UTF-8 that a downstream parser rejects
solution_text: Truncate on character or grapheme boundaries, and size database columns knowing whether the limit is characters or bytes.
source: public: UTF-8 is variable width; standard text-handling guidance

title: Sort order differs between database and application
context_text: Results ordered by the database appear in a different order after in-application sorting, because the collation differs from the language's default comparison
solution_text: Sort in one place, and set the collation explicitly where ordering is user-visible or paginated.
source: public: PostgreSQL and MySQL collation documentation; ICU vs byte ordering

title: Cron job overruns and overlaps its next run
context_text: A scheduled task occasionally takes longer than its interval, so two copies run concurrently and duplicate or corrupt work
solution_text: Take a lock the job holds for its duration and skip the run if it is already held, rather than assuming the interval bounds the runtime.
source: public: standard operational hazard with interval schedulers; flock-style guards are the common remedy

title: Disk fills with unrotated logs
context_text: A service becomes unavailable because verbose logging filled the volume, and the failure surfaces as unrelated write errors
solution_text: Rotate and cap log output by size with retention, and monitor free space as a leading indicator rather than waiting for write failures.
source: public: standard operations practice; logrotate and container log driver limits exist for this
